prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a polished 16:9 screenshot mockup of a fictional retro desktop operating system inside a pixel-art point-and-click adventure game. The user rejected ornate olive-and-brass game-themed window frames. Make this genuinely feel like a PIXELATED COMPUTER OS: practical late-1990s desktop interface, cool light-gray beveled window chrome, deep navy active title bars with white bitmap text, restrained teal desktop background with a tiny subtle repeating pixel pattern. Crisp hand-placed pixel edges, consistent pixel density, chunky small bitmap icons and legible bitmap system font. Absolutely no serif typography, gold/brass trim, parchment, fantasy ornaments, painterly scenery, cinematic gradients, or modern SaaS dashboard styling. No real-world company branding and NO 'Warewolf OS' or 'WarewolfOS'. Use only the generic title 'Desktop' where needed.
Layout: desktop fills screen, no physical monitor bezel or room background. Four tidy desktop icons aligned down left: 'Computer' with a tiny beige CRT, 'Mail' with envelope, 'Documents' with yellow folder, 'Recycle Bin' with small bin. Plenty of uncluttered teal space. One mid-size open Mail application window centered slightly right, with a navy title bar 'Inbox - Mail', authentic small beveled minimize/maximize/close controls. Under title bar compact 'File  Edit  View  Help' menu, small functional pixel-icon toolbar. Window interior light white-gray. Narrow folder sidebar 'Inbox (1)', 'Sent', 'Drafts'. Main area one selected message header and preview:
'Welcome to your new office'
'From: Building Manager'
'Nosh,'
'The keys are yours. Make yourself at home.'
'Good luck with the first day.'
Small 'Reply' button. Text clear and generously spaced at screenshot scale, no dense illegible text.
Bottom light-gray taskbar with a square icon and generic 'Start' button left, pressed active 'Mail' task button, compact system tray sound icon and '09:00' right. A separate small unobtrusive 'Back to office' control just above taskbar at lower right gives a game exit. No inventory, character portrait, quests, productivity charts, RPG meters or game dialogue box. Believable nostalgic desktop software rendered as beautiful crisp pixel art, cozy through the pixel craft, not through elaborate game-themed decorations. Finished game screen mockup, not a wireframe.
